title: A frozen RXTE size fit reduces NICER mean squared waiting-time error by 87 percent for 22 PSR J0537-6910 intervals
abstract: We test a known glitch relation with a frozen public snapshot. A line fitted to 44 RXTE intervals of PSR J0537-6910 predicts 22 NICER intervals with a root mean squared error of 21.46 days. A constant forecast gives 58.66 days. Mean squared error falls by 86.62 percent. A fit forced through zero gives 25.18 days. Small-event cuts, date perturbations, and paired block resampling retain the gain. All 23 NICER dates agree with the source table. Different instruments support transfer of the known relation. Shared timing methods, missing events, and cadence remain limits. A positive intercept improves prediction but does not identify a physical delay. No new glitch or planet is reported. Code, selected rows, source hashes, controls, and offline steps are included.

display.caption: A frozen RXTE fit predicts 22 NICER waiting times. Bars show quadrature date-error scales, not full forecast errors. The right panel shows residuals without a fit update.
